target_moa.text: Finerenone is a nonsteroidal, selective antagonist of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), which is activated by aldosterone and cortisol; it blocks MR-mediated sodium reabsorption and MR overactivation in epithelial (kidney) and nonepithelial (heart, blood vessels) tissues, reducing fibrosis and inflammation.

citations.quote: Finerenone is a nonsteroidal, selective antagonist of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), which is activated by aldosterone and cortisol and regulates gene transcription. Finerenone blocks MR mediated sodium reabsorption and MR overactivation in both epithelial (e.g., kidney) and nonepithelial (e.g., heart, and blood vessels) tissues.
Finerenone is a potent and selective nonsteroidal antagonist of the mineralocorticoid receptor that reduces inflammation and fibrosis due to overactivation of the mineralocorticoid receptor.

Kerendia contains finerenone, a nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist. Finerenone's chemical name is (4S)-4-(4-cyano-2-methoxyphenyl)-5-ethoxy-2,8-dimethyl-1,4-dihydro-1,6-naphthyridine-3-carboxamide. The molecular formula is C21H22N4O3 and the molecular weight is 378.43 g/mol.

key_safety.text: Most frequently reported (≥10%) adverse reaction was hyperkalemia (18.3% finerenone vs 9.0% placebo). Other adverse reactions more common than placebo: hypotension (4.8% vs 3.4%) and hyponatremia (1.4% vs 0.7%). Hyperkalemia led to permanent discontinuation in 2.3% vs 0.9% and hospitalization in 1.4% vs 0.3%.
